title: Impact of Technological Demands and Work–Family Conflict on Emotional Exhaustion in Knowledge Workers
abstract: Job demands associated with the use of information and communication technologies (ICT) in knowledge‐intensive organizations expose their employees (KIOW) to psychosocial risks. Drawing on the job demands–resources (JD–R) and effort–reward imbalance (ERI) models, this mixed‐method research (qualitative and quantitative) measured the impact of ICT demands (extended work availability, telepressure, and communication overload) and work–family conflict (WFC) on emotional exhaustion. This study also examines the role of overcommitment as a mediating variable on this impact and the degree to which e‐working effectiveness functions as a resource. The sample comprised 20 KIOW in the qualitative study and 137 KIOW in the quantitative study. It was found that ICT demands and WFC not only correlate positively with emotional exhaustion but also with e-working effectiveness and that overcommitment plays a mediating role between WFC and telepressure and emotional exhaustion.
